_about: Checklists used by the simulator. 'auto' items tick themselves when the cockpit really is in that state (scripts/core/checklist.gd); the others you confirm (Enter or click). Normal procedures and limits: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 flight manual. Emergencies: the student's AgustaBell AB206 manual E-AB206-250-1 Section 3. Quick cards: training website helicopter.daviesgarden.com. Always use your school's checklist and the flight manual of your aircraft.

lists.title: PREFLIGHT - EXTERIOR AND INTERIOR CHECK
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 2 Normal Procedures (Rev. 8, 6 Oct 2000) (condensed)

items.item: Cabin roof, transmission fairing, engine air inlet
items.action: Clean of debris, snow and ice
Oil level; filter bypass indicator retracted
Driveshaft coupling and temp-plates, oil level, mounts, isolation mount, drag pin
Engine, mounts, throttle linkage, fuel control, hoses, exhaust, cowl secure

items.item: Vertical fin, tail rotor guard, lights

items.action: Tie-down removed, condition, free movement; blades and tip blocks
Tie-down REMOVED (failure to remove it before start can cause severe damage)

items.item: Oil cooler, blower and access door

items.action: Reservoir oil levels, hub and yoke, pitch horns, pitch links, swashplate, control linkages

items.item: Cabin doors, windows, landing gear, left static port

lists.title: ENGINE PRESTART CHECK
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 2 Normal Procedures (Rev. 8, 6 Oct 2000)

items.action: Release friction; check freedom of movement; neutral / flat pitch, pedals neutral
items.note: Move the cyclic, collective and pedals through their full travel (frictions OFF, J panel).

items.action: Check full travel and flight idle stop; return to CLOSED

items.note: Overhead console (O key). The FUEL BOOST breakers are pushed in at their own item below.

items.action: TRANS OIL PRESS, ENG OUT and ROTOR LOW RPM illuminated
Collective up: light + horn ON; collective full down: light ON, horn OFF
Neutral / flat pitch, apply friction (if needed)
Circuit breakers in; fuel pressure in limits, FUEL PUMP light OFF
items.note: Boost pumps shall be ON for all normal operations (Section 1). The 206B-3 has no boost switch: the pumps run when these two breakers are in and the bus is powered.

lists.title: ENGINE STARTING
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 2 Normal Procedures (Rev. 8, 6 Oct 2000)

items.action: Engage (observe starter limits: battery 40 s ON / 60 s OFF, 40 / 60, 40 s ON then 30 min OFF)
Open to flight idle at 15% N1 with TOT at or below 150 C
items.note: N1 for the light-off: 15% above 7 C, 13% from -18 to +7 C, 12% below -18 C. Never start below 12% N1.

items.action: Monitor to avoid a hot start; abort if 927 C or 810-927 C for 10 s is about to be exceeded
items.note: ABORT: press IDLE REL, CLOSE the throttle and keep motoring with the starter until TOT is below 810 C.

items.action: Turning by 25% N1 (if not: ABORT the start)
If shut down more than 15 minutes: stabilise at idle for one minute before increasing power
ON (switch only: no radio simulation yet)

lists.title: PRELIMINARY HYDRAULICS CHECK + ENGINE RUN-UP
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 2 Normal Procedures (Rev. 8, 6 Oct 2000)

items.action: OFF, then ON (no uncommanded control movement)
Smoothly and firmly advance at a continuous rate to FULL OPEN, collective down, cyclic neutral
items.note: Rotor 50-60%: accelerate through this range as rapidly as practical (Section 1).

items.action: ON if OAT 4.4 C or below with visible moisture (observe TOT rise)
ON in visible moisture below 4.4 C
Centred, friction removed; move in an X pattern (about 1 inch), centre
Raise slightly (1-2 inches) 2-3 times, back to full down; check normal operation
Displace slightly left and right; note the higher force

lists.title: BEFORE TAKEOFF
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 2 Normal Procedures (Rev. 8, 6 Oct 2000)

items.action: Normal operating range, no caution lights

lists.title: ENGINE SHUTDOWN
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 2 Normal Procedures (Rev. 8, 6 Oct 2000)

items.action: Flight idle; check engine deceleration time (full rpm to 65% N1 in 3-5 s)
Stabilised at flight idle for two minutes
Depress and roll the throttle firmly to FULL CLOSED; hold it closed until N1 is 0 and TOT stabilising
items.note: Hold F at the idle stop for about half a second = idle release.

items.action: Apply cyclic to minimise static-stop contact

items.note: Aircraft with the fuel shutoff valve thermal-relief provision (Bell Alert Service Bulletin 206-82-18): leave the FUEL VALVE ON. Follow your aircraft's manual.

items.action: OFF after N1 is zero and TOT stabilised
Remain at the flight controls until the rotor has stopped
Install (high or gusty winds, other helicopters operating, or left unattended)

lists.title: QUICK CARD (website) - ENGINE START
lists.source: Bell 206 checklist, helicopter.daviesgarden.com/checklist.html (training website, not the official RFM)

items.note: Move cyclic, collective and pedals through their full travel.

items.action: ENG OUT, TRANS OIL PRESS, LOW ROTOR RPM on
Introduce fuel: throttle snap to the idle stop
items.note: The website lists this line as 'TOT - snap to idle stop'; it is the throttle that snaps to the idle stop.

items.action: Do not exceed 1 second over 927 C

lists.title: QUICK CARD (website) - ENGINE RUN-UP
lists.source: Bell 206 checklist, helicopter.daviesgarden.com/checklist.html (training website, not the official RFM)

items.action: Increase to full, keeping torque below 40%

items.note: No radio simulation yet: switch only.

items.action: If OAT below 4 C with visible moisture: ON

lists.title: QUICK CARD (website) - ENGINE SHUTDOWN
lists.source: Bell 206 checklist, helicopter.daviesgarden.com/checklist.html (training website, not the official RFM)

items.action: Reduce to idle, stabilise for 2 minutes
Off (FUEL BOOST breakers out on the 206B-3)

lists.title: ENGINE FAILURE - TAKE-OFF OR HOVER (skids below 8 ft)
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Maintain as the helicopter settles (do NOT raise it early)
Accomplish an autorotational descent and landing

lists.note: Do not restart the engine until the cause of the failure has been found and corrected.

lists.title: ENGINE FAILURE - LOW ALTITUDE, LOW AIRSPEED (skids above 8 ft)
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Adjust to keep rotor RPM in limits, establish the autorotation glide
If below 43 KIAS and height permits, forward cyclic to about 43 KIAS (code G)
Accomplish; touch down level, ground speed as low as possible

lists.note: If time and height permit before touchdown: BATT OFF, fuel OFF, shoulder harness LOCK.

lists.title: ENGINE FAILURE - LOW ALTITUDE, HIGH AIRSPEED (100 kt or more)
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Aft: speed-reduction climb, collective to keep rotor RPM in the red lines, climb until 50-60 kt

lists.title: ENGINE FAILURE - IN FLIGHT
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Full down at once, keep rotor RPM in limits, establish the autorotation glide
Accomplish (best glide 71 KIAS, minimum descent 42 KIAS, max 100 kt in autorotation)

lists.note: Never raise the collective to stretch the glide: it costs rotor RPM you need for the touchdown.

lists.title: ENGINE RESTART IN FLIGHT
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Open slowly to full open after the start

lists.note: Do NOT attempt a restart when the cause is obviously mechanical. About one minute to regain powered flight.

lists.title: EMERGENCY ENGINE SHUTDOWN
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

lists.title: ENGINE OVERSPEED
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Increase to load the rotor and keep engine RPM below the maximum
Power-on approach with manual throttle; if RPM cannot be controlled: throttle closed over a safe area, collective down, autorotate

lists.title: ENGINE UNDERSPEED
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

lists.title: ENGINE SURGES
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Power-on approach and landing without delay
Collective down, throttle closed, autorotate, fuel OFF, BAT OFF

lists.title: ENGINE COMPRESSOR STALL
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code
lists.note: If that does not stop it: land and investigate.

lists.title: MAIN DRIVE SHAFT FAILURE
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Open or adjust to keep engine RPM at or below the limit (the engine must run for tail rotor control)

lists.title: TAIL ROTOR MALFUNCTIONS (summary)
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Shallow approach 5-8 deg at about 60 kt, slow deceleration from 50-75 ft, use throttle and collective for alignment
Reduce power at once, hovering autorotation (rotation expected)
Reduce throttle and pitch at once, glide slightly above normal autorotation speed

lists.title: ENGINE / XMSN OIL PRESSURE OR TEMPERATURE
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Oil pressure drop, XMSN OIL PRESS or XMSN OIL HOT light, high engine oil temperature
Normal landing at the nearest safe area

lists.note: Do not continue until the cause is found and corrected. ENG CHIP DET light: power-on approach and land immediately.

lists.title: ENGINE FIRE DURING START (internal / hot start)
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: When back to normal: complete the shutdown, record the limit and duration of the hot start

lists.note: External fire: close throttle, complete shutdown, exit, use the extinguisher.

lists.title: ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Establish, prepare for a power-off landing
OFF (leave ON if lights / avionics are needed)

lists.title: ELECTRICAL FIRE / FUSELAGE FIRE / SMOKE
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code
lists.note: The helicopter can stay airborne with battery and generator OFF.

lists.title: FUEL SYSTEM / FUEL PUMP CAUTION
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Engine runs without boost pressure below 6000 ft (codes A-G); one pump is enough
With one or both boost pumps inoperative: 10 US gal

lists.title: ELECTRICAL POWER FAILURE (GEN FAIL)
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: CYCLE; if power not restored: OFF

lists.title: CAUTION LIGHT ILLUMINATION
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.item: ENG / XMSN / T/R chip, ENG OIL BYPASS, 20 MIN FUEL, HYD PRESS, FUEL FILTER
items.action: Normal landing at the nearest safe area

lists.note: Do not continue flight until the cause is found and corrected.

lists.title: HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FAILURE
lists.source: AgustaBell AB206 Flight Manual E-AB206-250-1, Section 3 Emergency Procedures (student's copy); helicopter code G values used where the manual differs by code

items.action: Adjust for the most comfortable control forces
OUT, check for electrical failure of the switch
items.note: Bell FM: HYD BOOST circuit breaker - Out; if power is not restored - In. Pulling it de-energises the solenoid, which leaves the boost ON.

items.action: IN if failure is confirmed hydraulic
As soon as practical; shallow approach, zero or 3-5 kt ground speed

lists.title: ENGINE FIRE DURING STARTING OR SHUTDOWN (Bell RFM)
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Section 3

lists.title: LIMITATIONS
lists.source: Bell BHT-206B3-FM-1 Rotorcraft Flight Manual, Section 1 Limitations (Rev. 3) and the student's AB206 manual for autorotation speeds

items.action: 810-843 C (6 s maximum; intentional use prohibited)
810-927 C for 10 s maximum; 927 C never (red light: 812-927 C for 10 s or 927 C for 1 s)
Accelerate through as rapidly as practical, cyclic neutral
About 20 US gal left (S/N 4110 and prior), 17 US gal (S/N 4111 and later)
40 s ON, 60 s OFF, 40 s ON, 60 s OFF, 40 s ON, 30 min OFF
Not above 4.4 C; ON in visible moisture at 4.4 C or below
Minimum descent 52 KIAS, maximum glide 69 KIAS, maximum 100 KIAS; level touchdown before NR passes 70%
Best glide 71 KIAS, minimum descent 42 KIAS, maximum 100 kt
